search_workflow_yaw.finding: Motor mapping and yaw direction agree in the pinned ArduPilot and Cosys implementations. The default 270 deg/s2 yaw acceleration exceeds the simulated high-altitude propulsion yaw authority while preserving vertical lift. The mixer can preserve yaw by reducing collective. Recorded reversals show large yaw-rate error, motor-pair saturation and real descent; this supports reducing commanded yaw acceleration, not suppressing thrust-loss warnings.
limits: This reduced model uses pinned AP command-shaping and AC_PID code plus a simplified yaw-only mixer/propulsion model; it is not a full six-degree-of-freedom flight simulation.
Tilt is held fixed; concurrent roll/pitch torques, drag, changing vertical demand, estimator error and actual network delay are not modeled.
A modeled lift/weight ratio of 1 is the zero-climb requirement, not a climb reserve or proof every saturation is eliminated.
Reduced acceleration makes turns slower; actual route, clearance, tracking and thrust-warning behavior require the operator live test.
No physical motor fault was established. No live result with the changed parameter is claimed.
